one_line_intent: On ThinkPad P50 with Quadro M1000M in hybrid mode, detect a GPU left initialised by the previous boot and bus-reset it.
generated_by: claude-opus-5-5 (in-session, same prompt contract as reason.py)

architecture_rationale.claim: BIOS does not always reset the secondary GPU between reboots in hybrid mode; leftover state produces spurious interrupts that disable the wrong IRQ (breaking the touchpad) and break nouveau.

evidence.excerpt: causes spurious interrupts from the GPU, which in turn causes us to disable the wrong IRQ and end up breaking the touchpad.

intentional_vs_accidental.claim: Reads MMIO 0x2240c bit 1 as a 'GPU was POSTed' signal, copied from nouveau.
pci_reset_bus() instead of a function reset is deliberate since the HDA function shares the bus.

evidence.excerpt: there are now two functions (the HDA controller and the GPU itself) on the bus, so the reset fails.

hardware_timing_dependencies.claim: Assumes undocumented NVIDIA register layout (BAR0 offset 0x2240c).

suspected_workarounds.claim: BIOS defect workaround with root cause unknown.

external_interfaces.claim: Interacts with the HDA controller quirk (quirk_nvidia_hda): enabling the HDA function changed this quirk's reset method.

evidence.excerpt: After b516ea586d71 ("PCI: Enable NVIDIA HDA controllers")

compatibility_certification_sensitive.claim: Gated on subsystem 0x222e and on reset support; also skips Dedicated mode where GPU advertises NoReset+.

evidence.excerpt: the GPU advertises NoReset+ when in this mode, so we can detect that and avoid resetting it.

reasoning.claim: Single laptop SKU; failure is loss of input device and graphics driver.

historical_lessons.claim: An unrelated quirk that exposed a second PCI function silently broke this one (reset failed) - quirks interact through bus topology.

evidence.excerpt: It previously used pci_reset_function(), and the available method was a bus reset, which was fine because there was only one function on the bus.
